unit.title: Manners at home, when no one is looking
unit.needIt: How you speak to the people you live with is who you are. Children learn it by watching, not by being told.
unit.why: A family that is rude to each other in private cannot pretend to be polite in public. If a mother only acts nice for guests but is mean to her kids at home, the kids will learn that manners are just a fake act. True character is built by how you treat the people you see every single day.
unit.outcome: Practice consistent kindness and courtesy with your family members.
unit.reachesYou: You see this when you are at home with your parents or siblings after a long day. It also shows up when you decide whether to be grumpy or helpful when someone asks you for a favor.
unit.do: Treat your family members with the same level of politeness you would show to a guest this week.

quiz.q: What happens if a family is rude to each other when they are alone?
choices: They cannot trick others into thinking they are polite
quiz.why: The text says families who lack courtesy at home cannot deceive others into believing they have those attributes.
quiz.quote: Families which exert neither courtesy nor charm when alone, can no more deceive other people into believing that either attribute belongs to them than they could hope to make painted faces look like "real" complexions.

quiz.q: What should a mother do if she wants her children to have good manners?
choices: Only be nice when guests are over
Show them the same manners she shows to company
quiz.why: A parent must model the behavior they want their children to adopt.
quiz.quote: A mother should exact precisely the same behavior at home and every day, that she would like her children to display in public, and she herself, if she expects them to take good manners seriously, must show the same manners to them alone that she shows to "company."

quiz.q: What is the greatest influence for good in the world according to the text?
choices: The home influence of admirable parents
quiz.why: The text states that no preacher can equal the influence of parents at home.
quiz.quote: No preacher, no matter how saint-like his precept or golden his voice, can equal the home influence of admirable parents.

quiz.q: What happens to a child's character if they see their parents do ignoble things?
choices: Their character can scarcely escape perversion
quiz.why: Children copy the behaviors and attitudes they see their parents modeling.
quiz.quote: If children see temper uncontrolled, hear gossip, uncharitableness and suspicion of neighbors, witness arrogant sharp-dealing or lax honor, their own characters can scarcely escape perversion.

quiz.q: Why is it a waste of breath for a father to order his sons to behave like gentlemen?
choices: Because he does not do it himself
quiz.why: A child will not accept a rule that the person giving the rule does not follow.
quiz.quote: It is a waste of breath for the father to order his sons to keep their temper, to behave like gentlemen, or to be good sportsmen, if he does or is himself none of these things.

quiz.q: What happens if a person only dresses well for guests and wears old clothes at home?
quiz.why: The text says that letting oneself slide into 'gray flannel' clothes at home causes a person to lose their mental charm and fastidiousness.
quiz.quote: The woman of charm in "company" is the woman of fastidiousness at home; she who dresses for her children and "prinks" for her husband's home-coming, is sure to greet them with greater charm than she who thinks whatever she happens to have on is "good enough."

quiz.q: What should a husband do when he returns home after a long day of work?
choices: Leave his business cares at the door
Tell his wife all his problems
Ask for sympathy for every small thing
quiz.why: The text suggests that a husband should put his business cares behind him as he closes his office door to avoid burdening his wife.
quiz.quote: It is a sounder practise for him to save her as much as possible from the trials of his business hours; and, incidentally, it is the best kind of mental training for him to put all business cares behind him as he closes the door of his office and goes home.

partials: Manners are tested daily at home.
Parents must model the behavior they want.
Home influence is stronger than preaching.
Manners should be identical whether alone or with guests.
crystal.key: True manners are a consistent habit of behavior, not a performance for others.

decoys.text: Manners are only for when you have guests.
decoys.why: The text says manners must be identical whether there is company or none.

decoys.text: Parents should only preach good manners to their children.
decoys.why: The text says a child will not accept a maxim that is preached but not followed.

crystal.aha: When you act the same way at home as you do in public, your manners become a real part of who you are.

scene.analogy: Guests for an hour, family all day

actors.label: Home is where manners are tested.

beats.say: Guests see you for an hour.
Your family sees you all day.
Company manners switch on and off.
Home manners are the real ones.
Real manners are a daily habit at home, not a show for guests.
